messages:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — ACME wants to add BYO-KMS + a low-latency streaming rerank step to the POC after the SOW was signed. Asked for impact + cost. 😬
Maria Gomez: Oof. Do we know QPS and expected RPS for rerank? Is this synchronous in the user path?
Alex Chen: They said ~200 RPS peak, avg 80. Must be <150ms p95 end-to-end for the critical path. It's user-visible.
Jamal Singh: 200 RPS with <150ms p95 + BYO-KMS = not trivial. If BYO-KMS requires customer-side network (VPC egress) we need private plane or dedicated capacity close to their VPC.
Katie Wu: Can we scope a reduced acceptance criteria for the POC instead of full production SLA? e.g., validate correctness and integration with BYO-KMS, plus a latency profile run (not full perf SLO)?
Alex Chen: They pushed back — execs want a latency demonstration. Sales asked for a plan that doesn't add 8 weeks.
Maria Gomez: Two options: 1) Hosted + mock KMS (faster) to prove rerank logic and quality, then show latency numbers in a limited dedicated slot with synthetic traffic. 2) Private/Dedicated trial with BYO-KMS hooked up — real numbers but longer lead time and extra cost.
Sean O'Neill: Estimate for option 2: provisioning Dedicated pool + network setup + KMS testing ~ 3 weeks ops lead + 1 week perf tuning. Cost: monthly reserved GPUs (min) or short-term burst infra — need finance to price.
Jamal Singh: For the rerank model path we can do a short-term speedup: quantize the model to int8 and enable prefix KV caching for conversational workloads. That can shave ~20-30ms per request in our bench. But quality tradeoff needs evals.
Maria Gomez: We should ask ACME for a small representative prompt set (50-100) and expected labels for rerank so we can run quality/regression tests post-quantization. Also, does BYO-KMS require HSM-level signature flow or just envelope encryption? Big difference for round trips.
Alex Chen: I'll ask for the prompt set and the KMS API spec.
DevOpsBot: Note: private plane onboarding checklist created: /playbooks/private-onboard.md (internal). Estimated env prep ETA: 5 business days once creds provided.
Katie Wu: Draft acceptance criteria proposal:
- Integration: BYO-KMS key wrapping verified with sample key (functional)
- Rerank correctness: Top-5 precision >= 0.8 on provided eval set
- Latency demo: single-node synthetic load: p95 < 200ms (demo only)
- Next steps doc: production rollout plan with Dedicated sizing + cost
Can we live with p95 200ms for POC demo?
Alex Chen: Customer prefers 150ms. If we can hit 170ms in demo they'll probably accept. Can we target that?
Jamal Singh: With quantization + caching + tuned batching, 170ms looks plausible at demo scale (80 RPS). At 200 RPS we might exceed 200ms without larger Dedicated capacity. We'll need to call out that scaling to full traffic requires capacity commit.
Maria Gomez: I'll scope a short eval plan:
1) Request prompt set + KMS API + sample data size
2) Run quality evals on float32 and int8 (report delta)
3) Do synthetic latency runs at 20/80/200 RPS on hosted + small dedicated pool
4) Produce a one-page risk/cost summary for the customer
Any other asks?
Sean O'Neill: Add network egress cost estimate for BYO-KMS flows and any TLS handshake warmup assumptions.
Alex Chen: OK — I'll get the artifacts from ACME today. If they refuse to share prompts, we propose a short proxy set.
Jamal Singh: Also note: if BYO-KMS requires mutual TLS and their cert rotation is aggressive, that will add complexity to the POC. Need their rotation cadence.
Maria Gomez: I'll draft the POC amendment and updated acceptance criteria and ping legal for a quick SOW addendum. Targeting 48h for draft.
Alex Chen: Thanks — sales will offer the two-path choice to the customer (fast hosted demo vs longer dedicated demo).
Katie Wu: Decision log: provisional — choose hosted + mock KMS for fast demo unless ACME insists on BYO-KMS wired to production keys.
Alex Chen: Noted. I'll update thread when I hear back. :thumbsup:
